category_title: Students with moderate to severe cognitive impairments who exhibit withdrawal or off-task behaviors in inclusive settings while thriving in self-contained environments
minimal_context: Katie is in a fourth-grade inclusive music class attempting to read music notation and play the recorder.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at the music notation on the board and play the next song on our recorders. Remember to use your fingers to cover the holes.

STUDENT: (Katie holds the recorder to her mouth but does not cover any of the holes with her fingers. She blows into it inaccurately.)

TUTOR: Katie, try to follow along with the notes and play with the rest of the class.

STUDENT: (Katie stops trying to play. She becomes withdrawn, looking away from the music notation, and starts just playing around with the recorder in her hands.)

TUTOR: Please stop playing with the instrument and try to read the music.

STUDENT: I need a tissue. Can I go to the bathroom? (Katie puts the recorder down on her desk, completely shutting down, and just sits quietly watching the rest of the class.)

options.A: Provide detailed instruction for each specific element of playing the recorder.
options.B: Ignore all undesirable behaviors exhibited by Katie during the music activity.
options.C: Avoid intervening too soon by allowing wait time for Katie to respond.
options.D: Have a peer point to the music notation for Katie to follow along.
